headline: North Korea test-fired an intermediate-range missile and claimed it carries AI features that let it dodge missile defences.
score_reason: A confirmed launch amid rising tension, but the AI claim is North Korea's own and unverified.
importance_line: A missile Pyongyang calls 'strategic', a word that implies a nuclear role, and says can steer itself past the defences protecting South Korea and Japan raises the stakes for people in both countries and for US forces there, but the AI and evasion claims come only from Pyongyang, which both allies say tends to exaggerate.
summary: Euronews reports that North Korea said on 4 Oct 2026 it test-fired an intermediate-range ballistic missile from Wonsan under Kim Jong Un's supervision, with Kim Yo Jong claiming the weapon can change course at low altitude and has unspecified artificial intelligence features that make it "extremely hard to intercept". South Korea's military said the missile flew more than 700 km and Japan put the distance at about 680 km, a gap Kim Yo Jong cited as proof it could not be tracked; the launch comes days after Pyongyang rejected Seoul's demand for an apology over landmine blasts that wounded three South Korean soldiers on 21 Sep 2026.
notes: Euronews text carries agency-style reporting; no other outlet credited in the text, so Euronews is the source.
